key_insight: DFT predicts that GeC/ReS₂ favors direct Z-scheme charge transfer, retaining the redox power needed for photocatalytic overall water splitting.
engineering_relevance: Tensile strain offers a route to tune this heterostructure’s predicted solar-to-hydrogen efficiency from 41.40% without strain to 60.68% at +6% strain.
method: First-principles DFT analysis of stability and electronic structure.
Band-alignment and Gibbs free-energy comparisons of type-II and Z-scheme pathways.
Evaluation of pH-dependent reaction energetics and strain-dependent efficiency.
evidence_signal: Calculations indicate a 1.38 eV indirect band gap, favorable stability, and Z-scheme pathways supporting HER at pH 0–14 and spontaneous illuminated OER at pH 4–14.
watch_item: The efficiencies are computational predictions; experimental validation of charge-transfer dynamics, catalytic performance, and sustained +6% strain remains necessary.
paper_title: Photocatalytic Water Splitting in GeC/ReS$_2$ van der Waals Heterostructures
